name: Persistent Placoid Maculopathy

criteria.description: Presence of persistent, large, yellow-white placoid lesions at the level of the retinal pigment epithelium and choriocapillaris in the macular region
Characteristic early hypofluorescence and late hyperfluorescence of placoid lesions on fluorescein angiography
Persistent hypofluorescent lesions on indocyanine green angiography corresponding to placoid areas
Exclusion of other white dot syndromes and infectious or inflammatory causes
Subacute onset of central visual disturbance or scotomas

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: All three major criteria plus exclusion of other causes are required for diagnosis
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis relies heavily on multimodal imaging and clinical exclusion of similar entities.

imaging: Fluorescein angiography showing early hypofluorescence and late staining of placoid lesions
Indocyanine green angiography demonstrating persistent hypofluorescence
Optical coherence tomography revealing disruption of outer retinal layers and retinal pigment epithelium
other: Electroretinography may show localized macular dysfunction
Visual field testing reveals central scotomas

distinguishingFeatures: Acute onset with rapid resolution of lesions
More widespread placoid lesions beyond macula
Lesions extend beyond macula in a serpentine pattern

redFlags: Signs of infectious or systemic inflammatory disease
references: Jampol LM, et al. Persistent placoid maculopathy: clinical features and imaging characteristics. Retina. 2015.
Spaide RF, et al. Multimodal imaging of placoid disorders of the retina. Ophthalmology. 2018.
